messages:
maya: Heads up — after the RBAC rollout last night a handful of customers reported SCIM failures and SSO logout not clearing sessions. Seeing 403s from the provisioner and logout loops. Anyone triaging?

samir: I saw alerts for scim-provisioner 403s at ~00:05 UTC. Logs show KMS decrypt errors for the provisioning token envelope. Quick paste: 
```
ERROR provisioning: failed to decrypt envelope: kms:Decryption failed: key not found (alias/redwood/scim)
http_request_id=abcd-1234 tenant=acme-corp
```
I suspect alias swap during the key rotation combined with RBAC deny on the provisioner service account.

alice: @maya do we have audit logs for KMS accesses around that time? If the key alias was swapped mid-roll it could produce transient errors and then SCIM retries might escalate to rate limits.

maya: I pulled CloudKMS audit — there are Deny entries from a short window: principal = serviceAccount:scim-provisioner@redwood-infra, permission = cloudkms.cryptoKeyVersions.useToDecrypt. Policy change rolled at 23:59 UTC. That matches the RBAC change window.

jordan: Also saw SAML logout oddness for the same tenants — IdP returned LogoutResponse with no InResponseTo and the SP rejected it, leaving sessions open. Might be two independent fallouts from the deploy. Logs: 
```
SAML: received LogoutResponse status=Success InResponseTo="" sessionIndex=xyz123
SP: reject logout: missing InResponseTo or binding mismatch
```
Could be that the SSO proxy and SCIM were on different versions during the deploy.

maya: Good catch. So two issues: KMS permission change causing SCIM 403 + SAML logout binding mismatch leaving sessions. Both correlate with the RBAC/deploy window. For KMS: revert policy or add explicit allow for scim-provisioner SA and rotate envelope keys? For SAML: possible mismatched config between auth-proxy and idp-client (post vs redirect).

samir: Triage plan: 1) Grant KMS decrypt to scim-provisioner SA temporarily so provisioning resumes. 2) Rotate SCIM tokens (re-encrypt) once KMS access is stable. 3) Confirm audit log entries and validate no plaintext token exposure. 4) Roll back auth-proxy to previous image to restore logout binding behavior while we investigate.

alice: For step 3, I ran a quick grep and found no logs with token payloads, only envelopes. Still good but we should assume compromise window and rotate. Also opening a vuln triage ticket to document timeline + notify customer success.

infra-bot: deploy:rollback started by jordan — auth-proxy v1.12.3 -> v1.12.2. Progress updates posted to #eng-deploys.

jordan: I'll keep an eye on logout repros. Can someone run this to confirm KMS allow? 
```
gcloud kms keys get-iam-policy projects/redwood/locations/global/keyRings/scim/cryptoKeys/scim-key --format=json | jq '.bindings'
```
If scim-provisioner SA missing, add binding: 
```
gcloud kms keys add-iam-policy-binding ... --member='serviceAccount:scim-provisioner@redwood-infra' --role='roles/cloudkms.cryptoKeyEncrypterDecrypter'
```

maya: I'm adding the KMS binding now and will keep it temporary until we rewrap envelopes with the new key version. Also will trigger a SCIM token rotation job and post results. Assigning follow-ups: @samir KMS policy audit, @jordan logout repro cases, @alice vuln triage & CS comms.

samir: Confirmed: after IAM binding change SCIM 200s returned and queued retries succeeded. No evidence of token leakage in logs. Recording timestamps in the ticket.

jordan: After rollback logout flows look normal in my test tenants (IdP post binding accepted). I'll run a small canary and confirm over next 30m.

maya: Thanks all — creating incident writeup and will schedule a short postmortem. Root cause = RBAC policy update + partial deploy ordering causing KMS deny and SAML binding mismatch. Remediation: coordinated rollout checklist for key rolls + deploy ordering guard. :white_check_mark:
